ai.description: The Manalar Night Frog is a small, brown amphibian with a snout-to-vent length of 20–25 mm. It features a distinct pointed snout, granular skin, and prominent, flattened toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus manalari* is best distinguished by its unique, significantly enlarged femoral glands in males, which are more prominent than those of similar congeners.
ai.habitat: The Manalar Night Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen rainforests in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Manalar night frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small invertebrates along the edges of forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus manalari* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of large, terrestrial eggs that undergo direct development without a tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Manalar Night Frog is endemic to the high-elevation evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Manalar Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard while perched on moss-covered rocks near fast-flowing streams.
